ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An object with mass $m = 1\text{kg}$ is placed on a fixed rough inclined plane with an angle of $\theta = 37^\circ$. A force $F_1 = 10\text{N}$ is applied parallel to the incline in the upward direction, causing the object to slide up the incline at a constant velocity. Here, $\mathrm{g} = 10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin 37^\circ = 0.6$, and $\cos 37^\circ = 0.8$.

1. Determine the coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the inclined plane.
2. If a downward thrust parallel to the inclined plane $F_2 = 5\text{N}$ is applied to the object, determine whether the object can remain in equilibrium. If not, find the value of its acceleration $a$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure is divided into two inclined-plane schematic diagrams on the left and right. The left figure is labeled Fig A; the block is placed on a fixed inclined plane with inclination angle θ, and the external force F1 acts upward along the inclined plane; the right figure is labeled Fig B; the same block is on an inclined plane with inclination angle θ, and the external force F2 acts downward along the inclined plane. Reasoning: First look at Fig A, and take upward along the inclined plane as the positive direction. The block slides upward along the inclined plane at uniform speed under the action of F1=10 N, so the resultant force along the inclined-plane direction is 0. The component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sinθ, and the sliding friction force is also downward along the inclined plane, with magnitude μmg cosθ. Therefore, F1 - mg sinθ - μmg cosθ = 0. Substituting m=1 kg, g=10 m/s², sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8: 10 - 1×10×0.6 - μ×1×10×0.8 = 0, 10 - 6 - 8μ = 0, μ = 4/8 = 0.5. Then look at Fig B, and according to the method take downward along the inclined plane as the positive direction. The component of gravity downward along the inclined plane is mg sinθ=6 N, and the external force F2=5 N is also downward along the inclined plane; the friction force direction is upward along the inclined plane, with magnitude μmg cosθ=0.5×1×10×0.8=4 N. Therefore, the resultant force downward along the inclined plane is Fnet = mg sinθ + F2 - μmg cosθ = 6 + 5 - 4 = 7 N. The resultant force is not 0, so the object cannot maintain equilibrium. By Newton's second law, a = Fnet/m = 7/1 = 7 m/s², directed downward along the inclined plane.
